candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is 'Acute-on-chronic liver failure due to acute hepatitis C virus infection,' which requires both the ACLF syndrome (hepatic encephalopathy, AKI, hypotension, decompensation on a background of cirrhosis) and the acute HCV infection as the precipitant. C001 identifies only 'Hepatitis C infection' without specifying acuity, the ACLF superstructure, or the chronic cirrhotic substrate. It is a component/cause of the full diagnosis but lacks the required composite specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Names the HCV infection component but omits the acute presentation, the acute-on-chronic liver failure framework, and the underlying chronic liver disease context

case_quality_flags: Seroconversion pattern (initial negative then positive HCV antibody with high viral load) supports acute HCV acquisition as ACLF precipitant in a patient with pre-existing alcoholic cirrhosis
Dental extraction three months prior is a plausible transmission event worth noting
